Written 2026-10-05 against extension@4.1.31 in a throwaway `create zip-probe --template=init` project. Ran `build --zip` (dist/zipprobe-1.0.0-chromium.zip, default browser chromium, dash stripped from the name), `build --zip --browser=edge`, `build --zip --zip-source --browser=chrome,firefox` (one source zip, one dist zip per browser, source Packaged line printed before dist and once per browser), `build --zip --zip-filename=release --browser=chrome` and `--browser=firefox` (release-chrome.zip, release-firefox.zip, NO release-source.zip without --zip-source), `build --zip --zip-source --zip-filename=release --browser=chrome` (release-source.zip plus release-chrome.zip), a build with commands.build.{zip,zipSource,zipFilename:'store'} in extension.config.js (store-chrome.zip, store-source.zip), `--output json` (zip_artifacts with kind/path/size), and a manifest with default_locale but no _locales (the manifest check error line). `unzip -l` confirmed manifest.json at the archive root and the source zip excluding node_modules, .git, dist and .extension-create.json. Exclusion rules, .map filtering and the symlink and not-created messages read from programs/develop/plugin-compilation/zip.ts and lib/messages.ts, clean behaviour from clean-dist.ts. Store rows read from developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/publish and /prepare (zip, 2 GB, manifest at root), learn.microsoft.com publish-extension and port-chrome-extension (zip in Partner Center, remove update_url, rebrand Chrome), extensionworkshop.com submitting-an-add-on and source-code-submission (.zip/.xpi/.crx, source package when minified or bundled, signed copy emailed), and Apple's distributing-your-safari-web-extension (app archive to App Store Connect or Developer ID notarization). Left out: the claim that Edge rejects a manifest with a top-level `key`, because neither Microsoft's publish page nor its manifest-format page says so (the latter lists `key` as supported).
